phases.2023: Groundwork: Lyon Square and the museum riverfront start, the Secchia arch is dedicated
phases.2024: Momentum: the amphitheater rises, the Butterworth trailhead opens, mussels move ahead of the rapids work
phases.2025: First wins: Lyon Square, the Cascade Road bridge and the Pettis South trail open
phases.2026: Big year: the Thornapple bridge, amphitheater and Rogue River trail open, rapids work begins
phases.2027: Knapp bridge, Cannonsburg west and Amway Stadium; the downtown rapids take shape
phases.2028: Ah-Nab-Awen reopens on a restored river; Ada to Lowell is the last big gap

stops.name: Fred Meijer Grand River Valley Rail Trail, Lowell end
stops.lead: Fred Meijer River Valley Rail Trails partners
stops.blurb: The west end of the 62 mile rail trail that runs from Lowell's east edge to Saranac, Ionia and Owosso.
facts: Begins at Montcalm Ave

stops.name: Fred Meijer Flat River Valley Rail Trail, Lowell end
stops.lead: Fred Meijer River Valley Rail Trails partners / LARA
stops.blurb: The south end of the rail trail north to Belding and Greenville, which starts at the 3.2 mile Lowell Area Trailway on Foreman Street.
facts: Starts on Foreman St east of Cherry Creek Elementary

stops.name: Fallasburg Park
stops.blurb: A historic county park on the Flat River north of Lowell beside the Fallasburg covered bridge, popular for picnics and weddings.

stops.name: North Country Trail Association headquarters
stops.blurb: The national office of the North Country Trail on Lowell's Main Street, which offers hikers trail information and restrooms. The Greenway is meant to join the trail here.
facts: 229 E Main St
National Park Service office in the same building

stops.name: Lowell Riverwalk and Flat River confluence
stops.blurb: Downtown Lowell's riverwalk along the Flat River near the Showboat, a short walk above where the Flat joins the Grand.
facts: Flat River boat launch and accessible kayak launch just north of the Showboat

stops.name: Lowell Recreation Park (former fairgrounds)
stops.blurb: The city park on South Hudson Street on the former Kent County Youth Fair grounds, with a boat launch on the Grand. It is the midpoint of the new Lowell connector trail.
facts: 225 S Hudson St SE
Fair moved to Deer Run on Cascade Rd about 2020

stops.name: Lowell to River Valley Rail Trail connection
stops.place: Lowell and Lowell Charter Township, MI
stops.blurb: A 2.2 mile riverside path with boardwalk and bridges that will link the township riverfront park to downtown Lowell and the rail trails heading to Ionia, Owosso and Greenville.
facts: Route: Along the Grand River from the township's North Riverfront Park east to Lowell Recreation Park (former fairgrounds) on S Hudson St, then on to the Fred Meijer Grand River Valley Rail Trail
2.2 mi path, steel and glulam timber bridges, culvert and boardwalk; MDOT let value $4.58M
Phase 1 North Riverside Park to Recreation Park; Phase 2 to the Grand River Valley Rail Trail
Design Williams & Works; partners Lowell Twp, City of Lowell, Kent County, MDOT

stops.name: Grand River Riverfront Park (Lowell Township)
stops.blurb: An 80 acre township park on both banks of the Grand west of Lowell, with sports fields, a splash pad, river overlooks, a fishing pier and a canoe launch. It is the planned eastern trailhead where Kent County launched its Greenway push in August 2025.
facts: South park 12200 Grand River Dr SE; north park 11998 Fulton St
About 1 mi paved path on the south side, about 2.5 mi of loops on the north
Hosted the Aug 19, 2025 Greenway kickoff

stops.name: Riverfront Park pedestrian bridge (Lowell Township)
stops.blurb: A long timber truss bridge for walkers over the Grand River that joins the north and south halves of the township riverfront park, stopping on an island midstream.
facts: About 600 to 650 ft
Built above the 100 year floodplain
Named for former supervisor John Timpson Sr.

stops.name: Ada to Lowell trail
stops.place: Ada, Cascade and Lowell Townships, MI
stops.blurb: The planned 9 mile final piece of the Kent County backbone, following the river from Ada to Lowell to reach the Grand River Valley and Flat River Valley rail trails and the North Country Trail.
facts: Route: Along the Grand River from downtown Ada east to Grand River Riverfront Park and the City of Lowell; alignment not published
About 9 mi
Partners: Ada, Cascade and Lowell townships, City of Lowell, MDOT, DNR
County said in 2025 it had about 65 to 70 percent of funding for south Ada to Lowell
Kent County asked the state for $5M in Apr 2026 (Lowell Township location, finish by Sept 30, 2027)
Design and fundraising underway in 2026

stops.name: Grand Rapids to Lowell south route (rails with trail)
stops.place: Grand Rapids, Grand Rapids Twp, Ada and Lowell Twps, MI
stops.blurb: A long range second route south of the river that would run beside the Grand Rapids Eastern railroad from Grand Rapids to Lowell.
facts: Route: Beside the active Grand Rapids Eastern rail line from the Grand River in Grand Rapids east through Ada (River St, Legacy Park, McGraw Park) to the Lowell footbridge and the Grand River Valley Rail Trail
About 20 mi; 2022 estimate $28.65M, unfunded
Needs an easement from the railroad owner
Listed as future in the 2025 framework

stops.name: Grand River Nature Trail and Preserve
stops.blurb: A 100 acre township preserve along the Grand with a 1.2 mile nature trail. The Greenway framework lists future river edge trail work here.
facts: 1.2 mi trail
Grand River Natural Area river edge trail improvements listed as future in the 2025 framework

stops.name: Ada Township Park
stops.blurb: A township park on Grand River Drive SE east of the village, with a picnic shelter, fishing and the parking lot for the Grand River nature preserve.

stops.name: Ada river access at Fulton Street (DNR)
stops.blurb: A public boat ramp on the Grand River at the M-21 Fulton Street bridge, just downstream of the Thornapple confluence.
facts: 621 Fulton St, Ada

stops.name: Fulton Street (M-21) trail underpass
stops.blurb: A planned trail underpass beneath M-21 that would link downtown Ada and the Thornapple riverfront to the Grand River and the state boat launch.
facts: Route: From Legacy Park along the Thornapple River to its mouth, then under Fulton St (M-21) to the DNR boat launch
2022 catalogue: $2.62M, 30% design, needs EGLE permit
Still listed near term in the 2025 framework

stops.name: Legacy Park
stops.blurb: A riverside park on the south edge of downtown Ada along the Thornapple, with a lower river path reached by stairs from the village.
facts: Joined to Covered Bridge Park and the new Thornapple bridge

stops.name: Covered Bridge Park
stops.blurb: An expanded 15 acre park on both banks of the Thornapple around the covered bridge, with a splash pad, playground, pickleball, dog park, veterans memorial, kayak launch and river overlooks.
facts: $8.5M Connecting Community campaign
Links Leonard Field and Legacy Park
Greenspace runs from the covered bridge toward the Thornapple and Grand confluence

stops.name: Chief Hazy Cloud Park
stops.blurb: A county park on Pettis Avenue with about three miles of Grand River frontage after land purchases grew it to 395 acres. It is planned as the Greenway trailhead for Ada.
facts: 329 Pettis Ave NE
Shelter, playground, ball diamonds, fishing and hand launch for canoes and kayaks
Master plan (2017) calls for trailheads, restrooms, equestrian and nature trails and a bridge to Roselle Park
Planned trailhead with restrooms and about 100 parking spaces in the Greenway catalogue

stops.name: Ada Dam (Thornapple River)
stops.blurb: A 32 foot hydroelectric dam on the Thornapple just upstream of the covered bridge, less than a mile from the Grand. No removal or restoration project was found.
facts: About 1.4 to 1.6 MW
615 ft long
Listed here as a river landmark; schema has no dam kind

stops.name: Pettis Ave Trail South
stops.blurb: A township trail along Pettis Avenue from Chief Hazy Cloud Park toward downtown Ada, set off from the road by a retaining wall in places. It continues an earlier Ada path from Knapp Street to the park.
facts: Route: Along Pettis Ave from Chief Hazy Cloud Park south to Vergennes, toward downtown Ada
About $2.5M from the Ada trail millage
Design Moore & Bruggink; contractor C&D Hughes
Project address 301 Pettis Ave SE
South end street named Vergennes in the source; exact OSM name of the end street not confirmed
Knapp St to Chief Hazy Cloud section was built about 2022

stops.name: Ada Covered Bridge
stops.blurb: A 125 foot rebuilt 1867 Brown truss covered bridge carrying Bronson Street foot and bike traffic over the Thornapple River just above its mouth. It is the centerpiece of Covered Bridge Park.
facts: Listed on the National Register in 1970
Rebuilt after a 1979 fire
Pedestrian only since 1930

stops.name: Thornapple River pedestrian bridge
stops.blurb: A new 270 foot bridge for walkers and riders over the Thornapple on the north side of Thornapple River Drive, joining Legacy Park and downtown Ada to township trails south of the river.
facts: 270 ft plus more than 200 ft of boardwalk on the south side (network page says 170 ft)
$2.5M: $1.575M trail millage, $500K campaign, $425K MEDC grant
Contractor Grand River Construction; design Progressive Companies
Project address 7421 Thornapple River Dr SE

stops.name: Cascade Road pedestrian bridge (Thornapple River)
stops.blurb: Upgrades to the Cascade Road bridge over the Thornapple that give walkers a wider path with a barrier, higher railing and lighting, near the Cascade dam.
facts: Funded by state ARPA and the Cascade DDA
Completion of both phases set for May 2025; final opening not confirmed

stops.name: Cascade Dam (Thornapple River)
stops.blurb: A 41 foot township owned hydroelectric dam on the Thornapple just southwest of Cascade Road. No removal is planned; EGLE limits seasonal drawdowns to protect mussels.
facts: About 1.4 to 1.6 MW, operated under contract
High hazard dam regulated by FERC
Fall 2026 drawdown suspended
Listed here as a river landmark; schema has no dam kind

stops.name: Chief Hazy Cloud Park equestrian trailhead
stops.blurb: A new entry drive and parking lot with trailer spaces serving more than three miles of horse trails in the park. Bikes are not allowed on the horse trails.
facts: 791 Pettis Ave NE
About 10 trailer and 20 car spaces
Horse trails with two bridge crossings
Construction bid $250,894

stops.name: Chief Hazy Cloud to Roselle Park bridge
stops.lead: Kent County Parks with Ada Township
stops.blurb: A proposed signature suspension bridge for walkers and riders across the Grand River between Chief Hazy Cloud Park and Ada's Roselle Park, to be funded by donations.
facts: Would join more than 600 acres of parkland
Listed near term in the 2025 framework; no date or cost published
Named in Kent County's 2026 state appropriation request

stops.name: Fulton Street trail (Ada)
stops.blurb: A planned 1.1 mile path linking Grand Rapids Township trails to Ada's network and the river along Fulton Street.
facts: Route: Along Fulton St from the west Ada Township line to Carl Dr, then to Grand River Ave
About 1.1 mi; 2022 estimate $2.53M
Status since 2022 not confirmed; may be built

stops.name: Roselle Park
stops.blurb: A 242 acre township nature park on Grand River Drive with over a mile of river frontage, paved loops through old pastures and wetland trails. The silos of the former Ada Beef farm still stand.
facts: 1010 Grand River Dr NE
About 2 to 3 mi of trails; restrooms open all year
Hosted a Jan 2026 Greenway open house

stops.name: Crahen Avenue trail bridge over the railroad
stops.blurb: A 140 foot weathering steel trail bridge beside Crahen Avenue over the Grand Rapids Eastern rail line, closing a gap in the township's trail network toward Ada, Kentwood and Plainfield.
facts: 140 ft; nearly $1M
Township has about 16 mi of trail
Not part of the Kent County Greenway program; whether it is the rail crossing Erik named is unconfirmed

stops.name: Cannonsburg Trail, Northland Dr to Chauncey Ave
stops.place: Cannon Township / Plainfield Charter Township, MI
stops.blurb: The western half of the Cannonsburg Trail, which will tie the Northland Drive trail and tunnel to the section already being built east of Chauncey Avenue.
facts: Route: Along Cannonsburg Rd NE from Northland Dr NE east to Chauncey Ave NE
Earlier releases expected a 2026 fall start; the Parks Foundation now says construction by summer 2027
Whole Cannonsburg Trail budget about $4M (Kent County and ARPA via DGRI)
Exact alignment and side of road not published

stops.name: Cannonsburg Trail, Chauncey Ave to Pettis Ave
stops.blurb: The eastern half of the Cannonsburg Trail, a roadside path toward the Cannonsburg ski area that meets the Pettis Trail and includes a small bridge over Bear Creek.
facts: Route: Along Cannonsburg Rd NE from Chauncey Ave NE east to Pettis Ave NE, crossing Bear Creek
Includes a small Bear Creek bridge
Design Prein&Newhof; contractor Bob's Asphalt & Paving
Partners Cannon Township and DGRI

stops.name: Pettis Ave Trail North
stops.blurb: A 3.5 mile separated path along hilly, curving Pettis Avenue that links the Cannonsburg Trail to Ada Township's trail network at Knapp Street. It is the last link in the White Pine Trail to Ada route.
facts: Route: Along Pettis Ave NE from Knapp St NE (near Forest Hills Eastern) north to Cannonsburg Rd NE
3.5 mi, 10 ft wide shared use path
Bid package: 18,100 ft of path grading, one pedestrian bridge, about 19,855 sq ft of retaining wall
Bid value $7.10M; network page lists $5.2M budget
Design Land & Resource Engineering; contractor Anlaan Corporation
Partners Cannon Township and DGRI
County bulletin says wrap up late November; Parks Foundation says opening winter 2027

stops.name: Knapp Street pedestrian bridge
stops.lead: Kent County Parks with Ada Township
stops.place: Ada Township / Grand Rapids Township, MI
stops.blurb: A separate steel bike and pedestrian bridge and raised boardwalk along the south side of the Knapp Street bridge over the Grand. It links Grand Rapids Township trails on the west bank with Ada and Cannon trails and the Greenway on the east.
facts: Route: South side of Knapp St NE from Grand River Dr NE east over the Grand River to Watercrest Dr NE
About 2,750 ft of pathway: 300 ft asphalt plus about 43 prefabricated steel sections
Main bridge about 575 ft; total cost about $10.2M (Ada Twp $4.4M, DGRI $4.6M, Road Commission $1.3M)
About 3,000 mussels moved in June 2026, including the federally protected snuffbox
Design Moore & Bruggink; contractor Milbocker & Sons
Knapp St closures expected in 2027; DNR boat launch sits at the bridge (2281 Shady Dr NE)

stops.name: Ada trail connection at the rail line
stops.lead: Kent County Parks with Ada Township
stops.blurb: Where the Knapp Street bridge path is expected to tie into the trail along the rail line on the west side of the river. Carbon marked it as the likely connection point; no published plan names it yet.
facts: Marked on the Carbon river map as the probable tie in for the Knapp Street bridge path
Not found in any county or township project list as of Nov 2026

stops.name: Rockford Dam Overlook
stops.blurb: A small downtown Rockford park on Bridge Street overlooking the dam on the Rogue River, right beside the White Pine Trail.
facts: No dam removal or restoration plan found in public sources

stops.name: Rogue River Park land addition (6624 Belmont Ave)
stops.blurb: A requested state appropriation for Kent County to buy state owned land next to Rogue River Park and add natural surface trails around its ponds.
facts: $438,500 request, sponsor Sen. Mark Huizenga, posted Apr 16, 2026
Not confirmed as funded

stops.name: Rogue River Park
stops.blurb: A 79 acre county park on the Rogue River in Belmont that doubles as the main White Pine Trail parking lot for this stretch.
facts: 6300 Belshire Ave NE
1.3 mi nature trail, restrooms near the trail entrance
Borders White Pine Trail State Park

stops.name: Rogue River pedestrian bridge (Rogue River Road)
stops.lead: Plainfield Charter Township with Kent County
stops.blurb: A prefabricated weathering steel bridge that carries the South Rogue River Trail over the Rogue River beside the Rogue River Road bridge.
facts: 175 ft long, 10 ft wide, concrete deck
About $800K to $880K of the trail budget
Rogue River Rd closed May 12 to 18, 2026 between Verta Dr and Woodwater Dr for crane work

stops.name: White Pine Trail connection at Rogue River Road
stops.blurb: The west end of the South Rogue River Trail, where the Greenway ties into the Fred Meijer White Pine Trail State Park near Belmont. From here riders can go north to Rockford and Cadillac or south to Comstock Park and Grand Rapids.
facts: Annual report lists the Rogue River Drive Trail as running from the White Pine Trail to the Rogue River Dr and Northland Dr intersection

stops.name: South Rogue River Trail
stops.blurb: A roughly two mile township trail along Rogue River Road that carries the Greenway from the White Pine Trail east to Northland Drive, including a new bridge over the Rogue River. It also closes the township's first trail loop with the Rockford and Jericho trails.
facts: Route: South side of Rogue River Rd NE from the Fred Meijer White Pine Trail east across the Rogue River to the Northland Dr NE tunnel area
About 2 mi, 10 ft wide
About $2.2M to $2.5M, paid by the 2016 Plainfield trails millage (its last project)
Kent County reimburses the township for the bridge
Contractor Dan's Excavating; engineer Prein&Newhof
Fully usable by May 28, 2026; final restoration and signs summer 2026

stops.name: Northland Drive pedestrian tunnel
stops.blurb: A 166 foot bike and pedestrian tunnel under the seven lanes of Northland Drive just south of Rogue River Road and 7 Mile Road, beside Blythefield Country Club. It links the South Rogue River Trail to the new Northland, Cannonsburg and Pettis trails.
facts: Tunnel 166 ft long, 18 ft wide, built from 19 precast concrete arches
Northland Drive closed Sept 25, 2026 for the arch install and reopened ahead of schedule (announced Sept 30)
Funded by $10M ARPA through a Michigan DNR grant to DGRI; county lists a $9M budget; bid value $7.47M
Design Prein&Newhof; contractor Kalin Construction
Partners: Plainfield Twp, DGRI, MDOT, Kent County Road Commission, Blythefield Country Club

stops.name: Northland Drive trail
stops.blurb: About half a mile of new separated path along the east side of Northland Drive between the tunnel and Cannonsburg Road, where the Cannonsburg Trail begins.
facts: Route: East side of Northland Dr NE from Rogue River Rd / 7 Mile Rd NE south about half a mile to Cannonsburg Rd NE / West River Dr
About 0.5 mi
Budget about $1M (Kent County, ARPA via DGRI and DNR)
Design Prein&Newhof; contractor Kalin Construction
One earlier county bulletin described it as leaving the tunnel's west exit; later releases say east side

stops.name: Indian Drive river access (DNR)
stops.blurb: A public boat ramp on the Grand River at Indian Drive, just below where the Rogue River comes in.
facts: 3277 Indian Dr NE
Part of the Lower Grand River Water Trail network of public access sites

stops.name: Grand Rogue Park and Trail build out
stops.blurb: Later phases of Grand Rogue Park that would add a pedestrian bridge over the Rogue River, overlooks, restrooms, more parking and a trail toward the Grand Rapids to Lowell route.
facts: Total estimate $5.8M in the DGRI project summary; Phase I $604,600 funded, Phases II to IV largely unfunded
Listed as near term in the 2025 Greenway framework
Current status of later phases not confirmed

stops.name: Grand Isle Park
stops.blurb: A 62 acre township park with almost 3,000 feet of Grand River frontage and an 18 hole disc golf course.
facts: 6266 West River Dr NE, Belmont
Course reworked in 2026 with no mow natural areas

stops.name: Grand Rogue Park
stops.blurb: A township park of about 65 acres where the Rogue River meets the Grand, built on a former campground, golf course and gravel pit. It has natural trails, ponds and kayak launches.
facts: 6400 West River Dr NE, between Jupiter Ave and Northland Dr
Opened Oct 2020
Only Plainfield park with access to both rivers; kayak launches were under repair after April 2026 flooding

stops.name: Donald J. Lamoreaux Park
stops.blurb: A 263 acre county park with about a mile and a half of Grand River shoreline, loop trails through woods and wetlands, and a river overlook deck.
facts: Entrances on Bailey Park Dr and Coit Ave NE
About 6 mi of nature trail

stops.name: Fred Meijer White Pine Trail, Comstock Park trailhead
stops.blurb: The southern trailhead of the state rail trail that the Greenway uses to link Grand Rapids with Belmont and Rockford. Trail users also reach it from Riverside Park in Grand Rapids.
facts: Route: Rail trail running north from Comstock Park past Belmont and Rogue River Park to Rockford and on to Cadillac
State park rail trail, Comstock Park to Cadillac

stops.name: Grand River Edges Trail, north segment (Ann St to White Pine Trail)
stops.blurb: The existing northern piece of the Grand River Edges Trail, separate from the downtown loop until the Leonard to Ann link is finished.
facts: Route: East bank from Ann Street north through Riverside Park to N Park St just north of I-96/M-37, then across a bridge to the west side to meet White Pine Trail State Park near US-131.
Part of the 5.4 mile Grand River Edges Trail
Wooden section and rough pavement noted by users

stops.name: Riverside Park
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation
stops.blurb: A large city park along Monroe Avenue on the river's east bank north of Ann Street, with a lagoon, paved loops and the city's accessible kayak launch. It is the northern anchor that the Leonard to Ann trail will reach.
facts: About 250 acres along the Grand River
Address 2001 Monroe Ave NE
Paved loops of about 2.2 and 1.5 miles; disc golf; two boat launches
2021 upgrades: restroom building, accessible kayak launch, lagoon edge plantings
Connects north via the Grand River Edges Trail to White Pine Trail State Park

stops.name: Riverside Park accessible kayak launch
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation
stops.blurb: A barrier-free dock on the Riverside Park lagoon that gives paddlers calm-water access to the Grand River. The city runs weekend kayak rentals here in summer.
facts: About $230,000: $150,000 DNR Recreation Passport grant plus $80,000 parks millage
Eight-foot paved paths from parking to the dock
Rentals Fri 4 to 8 pm, Sat and Sun 10 am to 4 pm in summer

stops.name: Westside Park (Ann St to I-96, west bank)
stops.blurb: A long-term idea for a 1.1 mile natural area on the west bank between the river and US-131 from Ann Street up to the I-96 interchange. No design exists yet.
facts: Listed in DGRI Greenway catalogue with cost TBD
Design not yet completed

stops.name: Former Kent County Road Commission site (Scribner Ave)
stops.blurb: A 14.4 acre riverfront site south of Ann Street along Scribner Avenue, picked to take the city services that moved off the 201 Market amphitheater site. The city parks office now lists 1500 Scribner Ave NW.
facts: 14.4 acres
City services from Market Ave relocated to 1500 Scribner Ave NW (Crain's, 2025)
Riverfront treatment not designed

stops.name: Indian Mill Creek mouth
stops.blurb: A west side tributary that enters the Grand River north of the Genesee and Wyoming railway. The Greenway list calls for habitat work and public access, with no design yet.
facts: Watershed spans Grand Rapids, Walker and Alpine Township

stops.name: Grand River Edges Trail, Leonard to Ann
stops.blurb: A new 12 ft multi-use trail that closes the gap between downtown and Riverside Park, and through it the White Pine Trail. Underpasses at the street and railroad bridges are left for a later phase.
facts: Route: East bank of the Grand River along Monroe Ave NW from Leonard St north to Ann St (project address 1529 Monroe Ave NW), with at-grade crossings at the streets.
0.75 mile, 12 ft wide
Estimated $9.1 million
Funding: City, MDNR, MDOT, ARPA via DGRI and MDNR, West Michigan Trails, private partners
Design Fishbeck and VIRIDIS; contractors Wieland and Anlaan
City said in June 2026 it was near halfway, completion expected December
Includes an interpretive plaza, lighting, benches, native plantings

stops.name: Adventure Park (former city water storage yard)
stops.blurb: A concept to turn the decommissioned water storage yard on the east bank along N Monroe Ave into a riverfront park with a canopy trail and playground. River for All once floated reusing a big tank as an event hall.
facts: Estimated $22.4 million, unfunded
Conceptual design only

stops.name: Grand River Upper Reach Revitalization (Sea Lamprey Control and Habitat)
stops.lead: Great Lakes Fishery Commission (decision maker); USACE Detroit District runs the EIS
stops.goal: Draft EIS expected July 2027; construction TBD
stops.blurb: The second phase would remove or replace the Sixth Street Dam with a new lamprey barrier and restore rapids from Ann Street down to just above Bridge Street. No design has been chosen.
facts: Extent: Ann St to just upstream of Bridge St

Seven alternatives under study: no action; fixed crest at existing site; adjustable at existing site; fixed crest about 0.5 mi upstream; adjustable about 0.5 mi upstream; fixed crest about 1 mi upstream; adjustable about 1 mi upstream
Public scoping meeting April 22, 2026; comments closed May 22, 2026
Over $20 million in federal funds committed to GLFC for a new barrier
Snuffbox mussel impacts add complexity; construction two to three years away at best (April 2026)

stops.name: Coldbrook / River North riverfront site (1101 to 1165 Monroe Ave NW)
stops.blurb: About 6.5 acres of city land at Monroe and Leonard, including the historic Coldbrook Pumping Station, that the city is offering for redevelopment with required public riverfront access. Greenway plans once proposed a park here with partly daylighted Coldbrook Creek.
facts: Parcels 1101, 1120 and 1165 Monroe Ave NW
Fire training facility vacates by June 2027
Earlier Greenway concept: Coldbrook Park, $23 million, creek daylighting and river access
John Ball Zoo aquarium floated as a possible use by a business group (not a plan)

stops.name: Canal Park
stops.goal: Opened late Oct 2026; official grand opening spring 2027
stops.blurb: A rebuilt east bank park in Monroe North with a playground shaped by Anishinaabe design, a heated rentable pavilion, overlooks and an accessible canoe and kayak launch. It opened to the public in October 2026.
facts: Address 905 Monroe Ave NW
Estimated $9.9 million (City, Monroe North TIFA, MEDC)
Half-mile renovation that raises the site and improves flood protection
Design VIRIDIS; contractor Owen-Ames-Kimball
Partner: Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians
Unofficial opening reported Oct 27, 2026

stops.name: Belknap Park
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation
stops.blurb: A hilltop park above Monroe North, upgraded in 2019. It is the uphill end of the proposed Hill and River Network.
facts: 30 Coldbrook St NE
2019: paths, restrooms, electrical, court and field upgrades ($540,859 plus $97,000 outside funds)

stops.name: Sixth Street Bridge
stops.blurb: An 1886 iron truss bridge over the Grand River at Sixth Street, the longest pin-connected highway truss in Michigan.
facts: 536 ft long
Built 1886; west truss shortened in 1921 after a canal was filled

stops.name: Sixth Street Bridge Park
stops.blurb: East bank park at the Sixth Street Bridge with a boat launch, overlook and sitting steps beside the Sixth Street Dam. A larger rebuild is planned around future dam work.
facts: Address 647 Monroe Ave NW (also the Upper Reach project address)
Existing boat launch, barrier-free loading ramp, fish cleaning station, shelter
Future Sixth Street/Monroe North Park concept: $29 million, terraced ADA bank, boat launch, pavilion, skate park; needs Spectrum land
Would serve as staging area for dam work

stops.name: Sixth Street Dam
stops.lead: Great Lakes Fishery Commission with US Army Corps of Engineers (Detroit District)
stops.blurb: The low dam between Fish Ladder Park and Sixth Street Park stays in place for now because it blocks invasive sea lamprey from about 1,900 miles of upstream habitat. Its removal or replacement is the subject of the Upper Reach study.
facts: Not part of the Lower Reach work
Removal depends on a new lamprey barrier still under federal study

stops.name: Fish Ladder Park
stops.blurb: A west bank park off Front Ave NW where a stepped concrete fish ladder sculpture lets fish climb past the Sixth Street Dam. A future upgrade would add trails, picnic groves and an emergency boat ramp.
facts: 624 Front Ave NW
Fish ladder built 1974 by artist Joseph Kinnebrew
2021 erosion control and path replacement
Future plan $4.1 million at 30% design

stops.name: 225 Michigan St NW riverfront site (USPS)
stops.blurb: A riverfront parcel just north of Michigan Street held by the Postal Service that the Greenway list flags as a development and access opportunity if acquired.
facts: Requires acquisition from USPS

stops.name: Grand River Edges Trail, downtown loop
stops.blurb: The existing downtown riverwalk that ties museums, GVSU's Pew Campus and the convention center together. It is the spine the Greenway projects are extending north and south.
facts: Route: Loops along both banks between W Fulton St and NW Coldbrook St, crossing on pedestrian bridges including the converted Blue Bridge trestle.
Whole trail 5.4 miles in two pieces not yet joined
Asphalt surface

stops.name: Ah-Nab-Awen Park
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids; partners DGRI and Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians
stops.blurb: The west bank park on historic Anishinaabe village and burial mound ground is closed as the main staging yard for the rapids work. A rebuild with accessible paths and river access follows the Lower Reach.
facts: 220 Front Ave NW
Closed from May 2026 through the Lower Reach project
Lower area (Bridge St to Gillett Bridge) rebuilt after Lower Reach; upper area (Gillett Bridge to Pearl) timing depends on funding
Estimated $6 million; design VIRIDIS

stops.name: Grand River Restoration, Lower Reach (rapids return)
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids with Grand Rapids WhiteWater; contractor Taplin Group
stops.blurb: Four low-head dams between Bridge Street and the Fulton Street bridge are being removed and replaced with two channel-wide rock grade-control structures, riffles and habitat boulders. It is the first phase of returning rapids to the downtown river.
facts: Extent: from 300 ft upstream of the Bridge St bridge down to the Fulton St bridge (some news describes it as I-196 to Fulton)
2,887 ft of channel and about 30 acres of river corridor
Construction contract $14,562,625.98 to Taplin; total spending capped at $25,982,101
$11,026,695 from USDA NRCS watershed program; NRCS finding of no significant impact Jan 2026
Staging at Ah-Nab-Awen Park from May 18, 2026; groundbreaking on Gillett Bridge June 1, 2026; in-river work July 1, 2026
Over 125 habitat boulders, three j-hook edge structures for slower access water; standing wave features dropped from design
By July 31, 2026 nearly half of one dam was out and a finished section near the Blue Bridge showed whitewater (FOX 17)
Work pauses in winter; second season summer 2027 removes the remaining dams
Target species: lake sturgeon, river redhorse, snuffbox mussel
stops.carbonNote: Carbon Stories has shot video here for the River Content log, with Dam 1 removal photos from Nov 2, 2026.

stops.name: Amway Stadium
stops.lead: Grand Action 2.0 with Kent County CAA
stops.blurb: An 8,500 seat soccer stadium on the west side near Pearl St and Mt Vernon Ave, a few blocks west of the river. The Greenway route is described as passing it.
facts: 230 Winter Ave NW
About $175 million; Amway $33 million naming deal
Home of AC Grand Rapids (MLS NEXT Pro) from 2027
Wikipedia gives groundbreaking as May 28, 2025; FOX 17 says April 22, 2025

stops.name: Gillett Bridge
stops.blurb: A pedestrian bridge between the Gerald R. Ford Presidential Museum and DeVos Place that links Ah-Nab-Awen Park and Lyon Square. It got a new deck in 2025 and hosted the rapids groundbreaking in June 2026.
facts: About 500 ft long, 25 ft wide
Deck replacement and railing work July to Sept 2025, $866,000 (City and DDA)
Stays open during in-river construction

stops.name: Lyon Square
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids with DGRI
stops.blurb: A rebuilt riverfront plaza between DeVos Place and the Amway Grand Plaza with a river overlook, shade trees and a heated snow melt drive, meant for year-round use.
facts: Riverwalk Promenade, 299 Lyon St NW
Estimated $10.3 million
Design Progressive Companies; contractor Rockford Construction
Groundbreaking Oct 25, 2023; DGRI expected early July 2025 opening

stops.name: Grand Rapids Public Museum riverfront
stops.blurb: The museum opened an accessible stretch of west bank riverfront with an outdoor classroom, direct water access and links to the renovated carousel pavilion. The opening slipped from April to June 2026 because of high water.
facts: 272 Pearl St NW
Riverfront portion estimated $12.2 million
Design VIRIDIS and TowerPinkster; contractor Owen-Ames-Kimball
Part of a larger museum expansion; phase 2 (lobby, classrooms) underway in 2026

stops.name: Grand River Edges Trail, Blue Bridge to JW Marriott
stops.blurb: A rebuilt stretch of the east bank riverwalk with bank stabilization, new plantings and universal access to the water's edge.
facts: Route: East bank riverwalk from the Blue Bridge (49 Campau Ave NW) south to the JW Marriott at Louis St.
Estimated $1.7 million (DDA and ARPA)
Design VIRIDIS and Fishbeck; contractor Katerberg VerHage

stops.name: Blue Bridge
stops.blurb: A former 1868 railroad bridge, now a pedestrian crossing, linking Campau Ave on the east bank to GVSU's Eberhard Center on the west. Restored whitewater was already visible next to it by summer 2026.
facts: 450 ft long, 25 ft wide
Built 1868, rebuilt 1892, converted to walkway after rail use ended in the 1980s

stops.name: Dam 2 boulder arch and cofferdam
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids; Taplin Group
stops.blurb: A cofferdam isolates part of Dam 2 so crews can build a boulder arch, the first rock structure of the Lower Reach. It sits where Carbon mapped the boulder install, beside the Blue Bridge.
facts: Cofferdam plus causeways built first in July 2026
Boulders started going into designed positions about July 30, 2026
Crews found a limestone slab with flow-cut marks they believe is part of the original rapids (July 2026)

stops.name: Fulton & Market riverfront development
stops.lead: Magellan Development with DeVos and Van Andel family backers
stops.blurb: A large mixed-use project on about seven acres of riverfront parking at Fulton and Market, including the former Charley's Crab site, with a public promenade and extended riverwalk toward the amphitheater.
facts: $740 million per Dec 2025 report (earlier plan was about $800 million, three towers)
Nearly 700 homes, boutique hotel, 53,000+ sq ft retail; $8.5 million to affordable housing fund
Greenway catalogue: Fulton/Market riverfront trail and edge, $5 million
Construction start not confirmed in sources read

stops.name: Riverfront trail, Fulton St to US-131 (incl. US-131 underpass)
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids with DGRI
stops.blurb: A later phase of the Fulton to Wealthy riverfront trail that would carry the path from Fulton Street under US-131. It is not scheduled.
facts: Route: East bank from the Fulton St bridge south along Market Ave SW riverfront, under US-131, to the start of East Riverfront Phase 1.
Listed as later phase on the Greenway hub
Would tie into Fulton & Market promenade

stops.name: Studio Park
stops.blurb: A mixed-use block a few streets east of the river with a cinema, music venue, apartments and a piazza. It is not on the riverbank but sits in the walk between downtown and the amphitheater.
facts: 123 Ionia Ave SW
$160 million; opened Oct 2019
Phase two: Canopy by Hilton hotel and offices

stops.name: East Riverfront Park, Phase 1 (Grand River Edges Trail, Fulton to Wealthy)
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids with DGRI
stops.goal: Fall 2026 (north part targeted spring 2026; south stretch end of 2026)
stops.blurb: A 4.5 acre riverfront park and half-mile trail on a former public works yard behind the amphitheater, with river seating, a kayak launch and a west gate entrance to the venue.
facts: Route: East bank from the US-131 off-ramp at Market Ave SW south past the amphitheater to the CSX railroad crossing (333 Market Ave SW).
$19 million budget; $18 million contract to Owen-Ames-Kimball (March 2025)
Design VIRIDIS
Funding: ARPA via DNR grant to DGRI, City, DDA, Kent County floodwall bonds, MEDC
Opening not confirmed in sources read as of Nov 2026

stops.name: Acrisure Amphitheater
stops.lead: Grand Action 2.0; Grand Rapids-Kent County Convention/Arena Authority; operator Legends
stops.blurb: A 12,000 capacity riverfront concert venue on the former city services yard at 201 Market Ave SW. It opened in May 2026 with a Lionel Richie show.
facts: 201 Market Ave SW
Final cost $184 million ($70M private, $114M public)
Built by Pioneer Construction with Barton Malow
Includes a nearly 4 acre riverside green ribbon

stops.name: Riverfront trail, CSX railroad to Wealthy St
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids with DGRI
stops.blurb: The southern unscheduled phase of the Fulton to Wealthy trail. City-owned land at 509 Wealthy is named as a future riverfront site.
facts: Route: East bank from the CSX railroad south of the amphitheater to the Wealthy St bridge, including a rail underpass.
Not yet scheduled
Future phases named: 509 Wealthy property, trail underpasses at US-131 and CSX

stops.name: 447 to 449 Market Ave SW housing and outdoor stage
stops.blurb: A planned affordable housing building of about 90 apartments near Wealthy Street with a small outdoor performance space and food trucks, meant as a link between the Oxford Trail and the riverwalk.
facts: About 90 apartments over a two-story garage
Depends on MSHDA tax credits

stops.name: Wealthy Street river access
stops.blurb: Planned river access on both banks just south of the Wealthy St bridge, with parking, an overlook and stair and ramp launches for kayaks and canoes.
facts: Estimated $3 million
30% design completed (DGRI summary)

stops.name: Wealthy St to Oxford Trail connector
stops.blurb: A short planned link that would join the river edges trail to the Oxford Trail on the west bank.
facts: Route: West bank, a quarter mile from the Wealthy St bridge to the head of the Oxford Trail.
About 0.25 mile
Estimated $1 million; 30% design

stops.name: Oxford Trail rehabilitation and extension
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids with DGRI
stops.blurb: A rebuild of the southwest neighborhood trail to the river plus extensions to Godfrey Avenue and Hall Street, with a playground, fitness area, small amphitheater and court under the Oxford St bridge.
facts: Route: From Wealthy St SW on the west side of the river, crossing the river and running south past Market Ave through Black Hills to Oxford St SW (trailhead 751 Oxford St SW), with new legs to Godfrey Ave SW and Hall St SW.
Over 1.5 miles of new and rebuilt trail
$9 million: $8M DGRI Greenway grant, $1M City ARPA
Contractor Erhardt Construction; design Progressive Companies
First major investment since 2011

stops.name: Plaster Creek Trail extension to Oxford Trail
stops.blurb: A planned extension that would carry the Plaster Creek Trail to the Oxford Trail and the river, giving the Third Ward and 49507 neighborhoods a trail link.
facts: Route: From the current trail end at Buchanan Ave SW (2509 Buchanan) west toward the Plaster Creek mouth and the Oxford Trail; alignment not yet set.
$1.5 million for engagement, planning and design only (ARPA)
Designer SmithGroup
Partners include City of Wyoming and Kent County

stops.name: Southside Creekways plan (Plaster and Silver creeks)
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation
stops.blurb: A city planning effort to turn the Plaster Creek and buried Silver Creek corridors into a connected greenway and trail system on the southeast side.
facts: Consultant SmithGroup
Public event March 11, 2026 at MLK Park Community Center
Some near-term projects planned

stops.name: Butterworth Trail
stops.lead: City of Grand Rapids / Kent County (Kent Trails network)
stops.blurb: A 3.5 mile rail trail that links the Oxford Trail area to Kent Trails and on to Millennium Park.
facts: Route: Rail trail from Kent Trails just south of John Ball Park and Zoo southeast to Oxford St SW and Norwich Ave SW.
3.5 miles, asphalt and concrete
Oxford branch reported closed during Oxford Trail construction

stops.name: Butterworth boat ramp (proposed)
stops.blurb: A proposed boat launch with truck and trailer parking off Veterans Memorial Dr near Butterworth St. The site is private and would need to be bought.
facts: Estimated $500,000; 30% design

stops.name: Kent Trails trailhead (Butterworth)
stops.blurb: A rebuilt Kent Trails trailhead near Butterworth that removed nearly an acre of asphalt, added about 90 parking spaces, more than 100 trees and a restored wetland.
facts: Kent Trails runs about 15 mi from John Ball Park through Millennium and Johnson parks to Byron Township

stops.name: Millennium Park
stops.place: Walker, Grand Rapids, Grandville and Wyoming, MI
stops.blurb: Kent County's 1,465 acre riverside park and the west end of the Kent County Greenway, with a beach, splash pad, boat rental and nearly 20 miles of trails. A new entry sign and landscaping went in at Butterworth and Maynard in spring 2026.
facts: New four season restroom and fountain 2024, playground 2025
Entry corner property bought with a DNR Trust Fund grant; house removed 2025
Replaces the downtown file's approximate millennium-park point

stops.name: Johnson Park
stops.blurb: The county's western Greenway trailhead, a 1928 park with about a mile and a half of Grand River shoreline. A $2.7 million upgrade added a four season family restroom, a new playground, covered gathering spaces and a bigger parking lot.
facts: 2600 Wilson Ave SW; about 224 to 258 acres
$2.7M total investment; contractor Spectrum
Partners WMMBA, Kent County Parks Foundation, DGRI, DNR (Trust Fund $400K)
Boat launch on Veterans Memorial Dr

stops.name: Indian Mounds Drive corridor study
stops.place: Grandville, Wyoming and Grand Rapids, MI
stops.blurb: A feasibility study of the four mile one way road along the river that weighed options including closing it to cars, to make it safer for walking and biking while protecting cultural sites and river access.
facts: Route: Indian Mounds Dr SW along the south bank of the Grand from Wilson Ave SW in Grandville northeast about 4 mi to Market Ave SW in Grand Rapids
About 4 mi corridor; nearly 2,000 survey responses in fall 2025
April 27, 2026 open house showed scenarios
Partners include Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians, Grand Rapids, Wyoming, Grandville, Road Commission, Metro Council, GR Public Museum
Consultants VIRIDIS Design Group and Fishbeck; ARPA via DGRI
Marker placed at the Grandville end on purpose; no sensitive site is located here

stops.name: Johnson Park adaptive mountain bike trails
stops.lead: Kent County Parks with West Michigan Mountain Biking Alliance
stops.blurb: About eight miles of natural surface trail built to adaptive and IMBA standards, from easy loops to features with a 130 foot vertical drop, opened with a community jamboree in October 2026.
facts: Route: Natural surface loops through the wooded uplands of Johnson Park
About 8 mi (grown from 6)
DGRI sub grant $540,000
Built by Spectrum Trail Design

stops.name: Grandville Grand River Waterfront and boat launch
stops.blurb: A 15 acre city riverfront on Grandville's north edge with a public boat launch, picnic area and a bike path to Kent Trails.
facts: 4745 Jenison St SW
Next to the M-11 (Wilson Ave) river bridge

stops.name: Secchia Gateway Arch at the Kent and Ottawa line
stops.blurb: An arch and small plaza marking where the Idema Explorers Trail from Grand Haven meets Kent Trails at the county line, near the Grandville clean water plant.
facts: Named for Peter Secchia, co-chair of the Greenway campaign

stops.name: Jenison Mill segment (Idema Explorers Trail)
stops.blurb: A one mile riverside segment that finished the trail link between Ottawa County's Idema Explorers Trail and Kent Trails.
facts: Route: Along the Grand River from Cottonwood Dr in Georgetown Township east to the Grandville clean water plant at the Kent County line, with a bridge and boardwalk over Rush Creek
About 1 mi
Completes a 3 mi run from the Bend Area to the county line

stops.name: Grand River Park (Ottawa County)
stops.blurb: An Ottawa County park with a Grand River boat launch west of the county line, reached by the Idema Explorers Trail. It sits just outside Kent County.
facts: Boat launch off 28th Ave
Bend Area to Grand River Park segment (3.52 mi) still in land acquisition
